strings.title: The Capricorn Killer
strings.hint: Who wrote about 'heaven's punishment' before carrying it out? Match 10:10 to the time of a decision that changed someone's life.
strings.solvedText:
The killer: Youssef Al-Kazemi — the horoscope columnist.

Youssef lost his newspaper job, and a committee that included all three victims rejected his City Observatory project. Its meeting ended at 10:10 in the morning — the time at which he stopped his victims' watches. Posing as an auditor, he bought a copy of Majed's security card, drugged his victims in parking garages and staged their deaths as astrological rituals. He leaked details to journalist Reema to spread the 'legend.'

The evidence against him: the rare ink in his observatory, the tower maps on his wall marking a fourth target, the gray wig, and proof that the anonymous-source messages came from his computer. The fourth target was rescued one day before the planned attack.
strings.summary.text: Three bodies in forty days, all businessmen found near the rooftops of city towers. Each body was accompanied by a letter in the same handwriting, a Capricorn symbol and a pocket watch stopped at 10:10. The third victim, engineer Tareq Al-Rouqi, was found on the roof of Al-Maha Tower. The rooftop door had been opened with a high-level access card, without force. The press has named the offender 'the Capricorn Killer.'
strings.summary.photoCap: Third crime scene — Al-Maha Tower rooftop
strings.summary.victim.name: Tareq Fahad Al-Rouqi
strings.summary.victim.note: Third victim in the series — the earlier victims' files are in Documents
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: Victim last seen in the tower's garage
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: Contact with the victim's phone stops
strings.summary.timeline[3].l: Investigators arrive and seal the rooftop
strings.scene.address: Al-Maha Tower — rooftop and helipad, floor 58
strings.scene.intro: An exposed, windswept rooftop with little sign of a struggle, suggesting the victim was drugged before being brought up. A stone holds the letter near the edge. The new rope has never been used — a carefully staged scene rather than a practical instrument of the crime.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Rooftop — evidence near the northern edge
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: Al-Maha Tower on the night of the crime
strings.scene.notes[0]: Rooftop door opened at 22:58 with a cloned high-level access card
strings.scene.notes[1]: A coffee cup containing sedative residue was found in the victim's garage
strings.scene.notes[2]: The third letter uses the same ink and handwriting as the earlier crimes
strings.scene.notes[3]: The pocket watch's hands were manually stopped at 10:10
strings.evidence[0].title: The Capricorn letter
strings.evidence[0].desc: The third letter: a Capricorn symbol in an unusual red ink, followed by one line: 'Justice descends from above.' The writing slants under steady pressure — a confident hand, not a trembling one.
strings.evidence[1].title: The stopped pocket watch
strings.evidence[1].desc: An old brass watch with its hands manually stopped at 10:10 — the same time in all three crimes. It did not belong to the victim.
strings.evidence[2].title: Climbing rope
strings.evidence[2].desc: A new, unused rope tied with a skilled figure-eight knot, indicating climbing or rescue experience. It is a staging element in the scene.
strings.evidence[3].title: The cloned access card
strings.evidence[3].desc: An RFID copy of a high-level security card. The original belongs to security supervisor Majed Al-Osaimi. It was copied with a commercially available device.
strings.evidence[4].title: The drugged coffee
strings.evidence[4].desc: A cup from the garage café containing a high dose of a benzodiazepine. Footage shows a man in a coat handing it to the victim.
strings.evidence[5].title: The three matching letters
strings.evidence[5].desc: Handwriting comparison confirms one author for all three letters, using the same rare ink and the same 'judicial' phrasing.
strings.evidence[6].title: Garage camera footage
strings.evidence[6].desc: A man in a long coat and hat carries an equipment bag at 22:20. He deliberately keeps his face outside the camera's angle — he knows where the cameras are.
strings.evidence[7].title: The synthetic hair
strings.evidence[7].desc: A gray synthetic hair from a disguise wig. The offender changed his appearance before approaching the victim.
strings.suspects[0].name: Youssef Al-Kazemi
strings.suspects[0].job: Horoscope columnist and former astrology consultant
strings.suspects[0].relation: Wrote about all three victims before their deaths
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'On the nights of the crimes, I was watching the stars at my private observatory outside the city — alone, as usual.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: The stars do not lie, Detective. Those three sat on the Development Award committee. They rejected my project and mocked my knowledge in public, so I wrote that heaven would settle the debt. I only wrote. I am a man of ideas, not actions. Yes, Capricorn is my sign, but half the city was born in January. Isn't it strange that a killer would sign with my star sign?
strings.suspects[1].name: Majed Al-Osaimi
strings.suspects[1].relation: Owner of the original access card
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I was on duty in the control room all night. The log proves it.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: I am drowning in debt. Two months ago, a stranger offered me ten thousand for a 'test copy' of my card. He claimed to be a security auditor checking weaknesses in the towers. I met him twice at night and never saw his face clearly: tall, thin, wearing gloves, speaking with a strange calm and quoting stars and horoscopes. I swear I did not know what he intended. I sold my weakness, not someone's life.
strings.suspects[2].name: Reema Al-Dosari
strings.suspects[2].relation: Reached two crime scenes before the police
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'An anonymous source messages me hours before each crime. My job is to follow the news.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: Since the first crime, an anonymous account has sent me messages coded with astronomical timings. I admit that I hid this to protect my scoop — a professional mistake for which I take full responsibility. I have now handed over every message. Whoever writes them knows details that were never published. He wants an audience and a stage, and I foolishly became his platform.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Saleh
strings.witnesses[0].role: Tower maintenance worker — found the body
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I went up at 05:45 to inspect the rooftop pump, as I do every Thursday. The man was lying near the edge, and the paper beneath a stone was flapping in the wind. I touched nothing. I ran downstairs and called security.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Amal
strings.witnesses[1].statement: A man in a long coat and hat came in at 22:20 carrying an equipment bag. He said he was the on-call elevator technician and showed a permit that looked legitimate. Later, I learned the elevator company never works at night. His walk was too calm — as though he knew the building.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Abu Salman
strings.witnesses[2].statement: I dropped an eccentric passenger near the tower at 22:05. Throughout the journey, he muttered about 'heavenly justice' and 'judgment descending from above.' He paid the exact fare in cash and left without saying goodbye.
strings.witnesses[3].name: Arwa
strings.witnesses[3].statement: A week earlier, my husband received an envelope with no sender's name. Inside was a sheet bearing a goat symbol with a fish's head. He laughed and said, 'The horoscope crowd has been angry with me since the award committee.' We never imagined it was serious.
strings.witnesses[3].items[0].label: Description of the envelope
strings.witnesses[3].items[0].text: A thick yellow envelope with no local stamps. The symbol was drawn in dark red ink. Arwa handed it to investigators, who confirmed that its ink matched the crime-scene letters.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Body discovery report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body:
Maintenance worker Saleh called the tower's security control room, then the police.
Rooftop entrances and upper elevators were sealed immediately on arrival.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Al-Rouqi autopsy report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body:
Death resulted from a high dose of a sedative that stopped breathing between 23:30 and 00:30.
No violent injuries. The victim was moved to the rooftop while unconscious.
Light friction marks on the collar yielded the synthetic hair.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Comparison of the three victims
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body:
The same substance and dose were found in all three cases. The staging is identical: a letter, a watch at 10:10 and unused climbing equipment.
All three victims served on the 2023 Development Award committee.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Third letter analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body:
The rare red ink is a handmade mixture of crimson pigment and gum arabic, not a ready-made product.
The paper was cut from a professional astronomical sketchbook.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Cloned card examination
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body:
The card was copied using a commercial RFID device available online.
The original card number belongs to security supervisor Majed Al-Osaimi, who never reported it missing.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Rope knot report
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body:
An expertly tied figure-eight knot.
The rope is completely new, purchased with cash and difficult to trace.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Rooftop access log
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body:
Rooftop door opened at 22:58 with a high-level access card (a copy).
No further opening until 05:45 the following morning.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Garage camera report
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body:
At 22:20, a man in a long coat and hat carries an equipment bag and precisely avoids the camera angles.
He is seen handing the victim a coffee near the elevator.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Victim's call log
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body:
The last call came from a deactivated number at 21:55 and lasted 40 seconds.
The number belongs to the same type of temporary SIM used in the two earlier crimes.
strings.folders[3].docs[3].title: 'The Stars Rule' column archive
strings.folders[3].docs[3].body:
Three old articles by Youssef Al-Kazemi attacked the victims by name after the committee's decision, threatening them with 'heaven's just judgment descending from above.'
The phrasing almost exactly matches the line in the letters.
strings.folders[4].name: Interviews
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Youssef Al-Kazemi interview
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body:
Unnaturally calm. Answers with astrological sayings and knows the timings in striking detail.
Refused a voluntary search of the observatory. A search warrant was obtained.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Majed Al-Osaimi interview
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body:
Broke down and disclosed the 'test copy' deal for 10 thousand.
Described the buyer as tall and thin, wearing gloves and speaking calmly about astrology. Fully cooperated with the composite sketch.
strings.folders[4].docs[2].title: Reema Al-Dosari interview
strings.folders[4].docs[2].body:
After initial reluctance, she handed over every message from the anonymous source.
They arrive hours before each crime and contain astronomical coordinates indicating the location.
strings.folders[4].docs[3].title: Amal's interview — reception
strings.folders[4].docs[3].body:
Described the nighttime 'elevator technician' and his fake permit.
Later recognized his voice with high confidence in an old television clip of Al-Kazemi.
strings.folders[5].name: Court orders
strings.folders[5].docs[0].title: Private observatory search warrant
strings.folders[5].docs[0].body: Authorization to search Al-Kazemi's observatory outside the city and seize equipment, papers and inks.
strings.folders[5].docs[1].title: Order to trace the anonymous account
strings.folders[5].docs[1].body: Court order to trace the source of the anonymous messages sent to the journalist.
strings.folders[6].name: Classified files
strings.folders[6].docs[0].title: Fourth target map
strings.folders[6].docs[0].body:
A map of the city's towers was found in the observatory, with Al-Nakheel Tower circled in red and dated 22 October — the fourth committee member.
The target was secured and surveillance deployed one day before the planned attack.
strings.folders[6].docs[1].title: Message-source computer analysis
strings.folders[6].docs[1].body:
The anonymous-source messages were sent from the observatory's own computer through a masked network.
The gray wig and long coat were found in the observatory wardrobe.
strings.reports[0].title: Criminal behavior unit report
strings.reports[0].author: Behavioral analysis unit
strings.reports[0].body:
An organized killer driven by narcissistic revenge, using astrological symbolism to present the crimes as 'divine judgment.'
He needs an audience. Leaking details to the press is part of the ritual.
The time 10:10 is a personal key: look for a professional event at that time.
strings.reports[1].title: Rooftop scene report
strings.reports[1].author: Scene examination team
strings.reports[1].body:
No signs of a struggle on the rooftop. The victim was dragged from the service elevator to the helipad.
The rope, letter and watch were carefully staged just before or after death.
strings.reports[2].title: Report linking the three crimes
strings.reports[2].author: Serial case operations team
strings.reports[2].body:
The victims' only shared connection was membership of the 2023 Development Award committee, which rejected the City Observatory project and revoked its creator's accreditation.
The fourth committee member is under protection.
strings.notes[0].text: 10:10 is no coincidence — find an event at that time
strings.notes[1].text: Who benefited from publishing the details? Who leaked them?
strings.notes[2].text: Development Award committee: three dead… who is the fourth?
